# Chapter 18 — Document Lifecycle and Canon Supremacy

The UIAO document lifecycle management guide codifies the governance of governance — the processes that ensure the UIAO corpus itself is created, versioned, reviewed, approved, updated, deprecated, and archived with the same rigor that UIAO applies to the modernization artifacts it governs. This recursive governance requirement is not an afterthought. A governance program that cannot govern its own documentation is a governance program that will drift from its own standards, producing the exact failure mode — undocumented decisions, inconsistent standards, orphaned artifacts — that it was designed to prevent in the production environment.

The foundational principle is canon supremacy: the canon/ directory in the UIAO governance repository is the single authoritative source of truth, and every derived artifact — rendered HTML, compliance dashboard, OrgPath calculation, migration plan — must trace its provenance directly to a canonical governance record committed to that directory. Documents in the corpus carry immutable UIAO-NNN identifiers assigned sequentially at creation and never reused, even after a document is archived. Version numbering follows semantic versioning conventions adapted for governance documents: major version increments for structural changes that invalidate previous implementations and require re-execution of dependent workflows; minor version increments for content additions that do not break compatibility with existing implementations; and patch version increments for corrections and clarifications that do not change the normative requirements of the document.

Document status follows a six-state lifecycle enforced by the Git hook infrastructure. DRAFT status is the initial state for all new documents, permitting unrestricted editing without Canon Steward review. IN_REVIEW status locks the document against direct commits, requiring all changes to proceed through pull requests with a designated reviewer. APPROVED status indicates Canon Steward sign-off and permits commitment to the canon/ directory. CURRENT status is the operational state for documents actively used in production governance workflows. DEPRECATED status signals that a document has been superseded and should not be used for new work, while remaining accessible for reference. ARCHIVED status removes the document from active governance workflows while preserving it in the repository history for audit purposes.

YAML frontmatter is mandatory on every document and is validated by Git pre-receive hooks before any commit can be accepted into the repository. The frontmatter schema requires nine fields: document_id, version, status, classification, boundary, owner, created, last_updated, review_cadence, and repository. The classification and boundary fields are validated against an enumerated set of permitted values defined in the governance hook configuration — any document that claims a classification or boundary designation not in the approved set is rejected at the hook layer, producing a clear error message that identifies the invalid field value and the permitted alternatives. This enforcement mechanism ensures that no document can enter the canonical record with a classification claim that has not been authorized by the governance framework.

The Copilot Tasks integration is explicitly documented as a governance-compliant document regeneration tool within the lifecycle framework. AI-assisted document regeneration is permitted subject to a mandatory human-in-the-loop review at every lifecycle gate. An AI-generated document must be reviewed and approved by a Canon Steward before it can transition from IN_REVIEW to APPROVED status, and the pull request template for AI-generated content requires the reviewing Canon Steward to attest explicitly that they have read the complete document, verified its technical accuracy against the assessed environment data, and confirmed its compliance with UIAO document standards. This attestation requirement ensures that AI assistance accelerates document production without reducing the quality or accountability of the governance record.
